clue.text: Plain-speaking genius ignoring one gothic novel

indicators.note: to ignore one is to leave out a single 'I', the letter standing for one

parts.note: someone frank speaks plainly
Albert Einstein, the byword for genius

explanation.surface: A blunt, brilliant author leaves something out of a gothic novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' is the letter I here, and only the first of the genius's two I's is dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: Mary Shelley's Frankenstein is the classic gothic horror novel of 1818.

indicators.note: something crushed is squashed out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A metal carton gets squashed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is' looks like part of the verb 'is crushed', but it belongs to the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Cast iron is an iron alloy poured into moulds, a common metal.

indicators.note: something revolutionary turns over, so the word is read from the end backwards

parts.note: bats is slang for mad

explanation.surface: A mad rebel wielding a knife.
explanation.definitionFit: To knife someone is to stab them; both are verbs of wounding with a blade.

clue.text: Flower close to capstan at the back of a ship

definitions.text: at the back of a ship

parts.note: the aster is a daisy-like flower

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only its final letter is kept

parts.note: the final letter of capstan

explanation.surface: A flower lies near the capstan at a ship's stern.
explanation.walkthrough: A capstan is the winch on a ship's deck, which makes 'Flower' read as a deck ornament rather than wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Astern is the nautical term for behind or towards the rear of a vessel.

parts.note: to train someone is to instruct them
E.T., the film's extra-terrestrial

explanation.surface: Someone teaches a visitor from space how to make a plaything.
explanation.definitionFit: A train set is a model railway, a classic children's plaything.

indicators.note: made brief means cut short, so the word's last letter is dropped

parts.note: to study is to examine closely

explanation.surface: Take a quick look at an earring.
explanation.definitionFit: A stud is a small earring fixed through the lobe by a post.

indicators.note: letters that are moving shift about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A shout of alarm as a crate starts to slide.
explanation.definitionFit: To react is to respond with some action, as an urgent call for a response demands.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to extend or draw out

definitions.note: a noun phrase: 'a stretch' is a term inside
definitions.meaning: second meaning: slang for a term of imprisonment

explanation.surface: Someone's time behind bars is extended.
explanation.definitionFit: Stretch means to make longer, and is also criminal slang for a period served in jail.

parts.note: a judge hears or tries a case
a post going viral is trending online

explanation.surface: An attempt to make something spread online ends sadly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Try' reads as 'attempt'; it is the courtroom sense, to hear a case.
explanation.definitionFit: Something heart-rending causes deep grief, which is what a tragic event does.

indicators.note: one word accepting another takes it inside itself

parts.note: a noble is a member of the aristocracy
ta is informal British for thanks

explanation.surface: An unusual lord who actually says thank you.
explanation.definitionFit: Notable means worth noticing, a close synonym of remarkable.

parts.note: in means in fashion

indicators.note: going backward means the word is read from its end to its start

parts.note: to aid is to help

explanation.surface: It is trendy to give aid to a developing nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backward country' looks like an insult to the nation; 'backward' applies only to the word for help.
explanation.definitionFit: India is a country in South Asia.

parts.note: Wyatt Earp, the Wild West marshal
to hone a skill is to perfect it

explanation.surface: A US sheriff polishing his surveillance gear.
explanation.definitionFit: Earphones are worn on or in the ears to listen to audio.

clue.text: Bad weather to spoil finale of wordy prayer

parts.note: hail is a fall of ice pellets
to mar is to spoil

indicators.note: a finale is the ending, so only the final letter is kept

parts.note: the last letter of wordy

explanation.surface: A storm ruins the end of a long-winded prayer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hail Mary is the Catholic devotion to the Virgin, beginning with the angel's greeting.

indicators.note: occasionally means every so often, so only every other letter is taken

parts.note: first, third and fifth letters of crafty

explanation.surface: A pet that is sometimes sly.
explanation.definitionFit: The cat is one of the commonest household pets.

indicators.note: one word is put with another outside it, so the second wraps round the first
the wine sits outside, so it wraps around the other piece

parts.note: claret is red Bordeaux wine
at home means in

explanation.surface: An order to leave the wine out of the house.
explanation.definitionFit: The clarinet is a single-reed woodwind instrument.

indicators.note: a word not finished stops short, so its last letter is lost

parts.note: a ditty is a simple song

explanation.surface: A youngster's little song is left incomplete.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'Child's' reads as a possessive but stands for 'is', linking definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A son is a male child of his parents.

clue.text: Uncomfortable, Bill ate a seafood sample

indicators.note: a sample is a small part taken from the whole, so the letters come from inside the phrase

parts.note: runs from inside Bill to the start of seafood

explanation.surface: Bill felt queasy after trying some seafood.
explanation.definitionFit: To be ill at ease is to feel awkward or uncomfortable.

indicators.note: one word placed in another sits inside it

parts.note: a log is a record, as a ship's log
a sin is a wrongdoing

explanation.surface: Someone has mislaid a misdeed noted down in a register.
explanation.definitionFit: Losing something is mislaying it, so it is misplacing in the same participle form.

indicators.note: something composed is put together anew, so the letters are arranged in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Verses written about a horse-racing venue.
explanation.walkthrough: Epsom Downs, in Surrey, is the English racecourse where the Derby is run.
explanation.definitionFit: Epsom is a famous English racecourse, home of the Derby horse race.

clue.text: Style of music from Asian capital overheard

parts.note: Seoul is the capital of South Korea

explanation.surface: A kind of music heard drifting from a city in Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: Soul is a genre of African-American popular music rooted in gospel and rhythm and blues.

clue.text: Bread is tossed for gull, say

indicators.note: things tossed are thrown about and land in a different order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Bread is thrown to a gull at the seaside.
explanation.definitionFit: A gull is one example of a bird of the coast, signalled by 'say'.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: playfully knowing or roguish

explanation.surface: A naughty head teacher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Principal' tempts as a noun, the head of a school; here it is the adjective chief.
explanation.definitionFit: Arch means roguishly playful as an adjective, and also chief or leading, as in archbishop.

clue.text: Particle of dirt ultimately found in nerve cell

indicators.note: a thing found in something lies inside it

parts.note: a neuron is a nerve cell

parts.note: the last letter of dirt

explanation.surface: A speck of grime discovered inside a nerve cell.
explanation.definitionFit: A neutron is an uncharged subatomic particle in the atomic nucleus.

indicators.note: something broken is in pieces that can be reassembled differently

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Cleaning up a shattered spear.
